usageNotes: Use this to inspect the full OpenID Connect configuration for a specific realm before modifying it or troubleshooting SSO login failures. The caller must hold the System.Audit privilege on /access/domains — API tokens are supported. Note that client-key (the client secret) is returned in the response, so treat the output as sensitive.

examples.summary: Retrieve the configuration for an OpenID realm named 'sso-azure'

tips: The realm name must be 2–32 characters and match /^(?:[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._\-]*)$/ — names starting with a dot or hyphen are rejected.
client-key (the OIDC client secret) is included in the response; avoid logging or storing the output in plain text.
If autocreate is false and a user does not yet exist in PDM, their first SSO login will fail even if the IdP authenticates them successfully.
scopes defaults to 'email profile'; if username-claim references a non-standard claim (e.g. 'preferred_username'), ensure that scope is included in the realm config.
Use this endpoint to capture the current state before calling the corresponding update operation, so you can diff and restore if needed.
